bitfield.description: Command mailbox location. Once a command arrives, the fields from the opcode are dumped contiguously on this address. Aside from the opcode and length which are given in system endianness, the remainder of the command is in the endianness of the host.
Set to "1" by NAB H/W, when a new command arrives. Set to "0" by S/W (by actualy writing "1" to it, i.e. Write Clear) when the corresponding event has been submitted to NAB.

Event mailbox location. S/W fills this block with data, including opcode and len fields, to be sent to the host in the appropriate cnys request. The len field must include the Rx status field, i.e., must be +4 then the remainder of the packet in the event mailbox.

Nab supports adding info words toward host during event mailbox response. This field Indicates the source of word nr. 1: "0" - feature disabled (do not add any word). Nab transfers mailbox As-is. "1" - source is nab_srp_skt_not_empty_vec - the monitored-only Rx FIFO non-empty sockets (note that monitored sockets are configured in MEM_SRP_SKT_MONITORED_VEC) "2" - source is timer count. i.e. the always-on-domain counter is used. "3-6" - TBD "7" - source is an OCP mapped memory read (mostly for reading any register which is not mapped by index 1 to 6)

Set to "1" by S/W, when the event address and length are filled up with a new event. Note that the NAB H/W then signals the host (IRQ line) when this is set, to ask the host to issue cnys request. Set to "0" by NAB, when the event has been fully consumed by the host.

Nab supports adding info words toward host during event mailbox response. This field Indicates the source of word nr. 2: "0" - feature disabled (do not add any word). Nab transfers mailbox As-is. "1" - source is nab_srp_skt_not_empty_vec - the monitored-only Rx FIFO non-empty sockets (note that monitored sockets are configured in MEM_SRP_SKT_MONITORED_VEC) "2" - source is timer count. i.e. the always-on-domain counter is used. "3-6" - TBD "7" - source is an OCP mapped memory read (mostly for reading any register which is not mapped by index 1 to 6)

Indicates the added word nr.1 (if exists) offset location within the response sequence: "0" - N.A (this is OP-LEN field offset location) "1" - Place word nr.1 in word offset 1 (right after OP-LEN field) "2" - Place word nr.1 in word offset 2 "3" - Place word nr.1 in word offset 3 etc...

Indicates the added word nr.2 (if exists) offset location within the response sequence: "0" - N.A (this is OP-LEN field offset location) "1" - Place word nr.2 in word offset 1 (right after OP-LEN field) "2" - Place word nr.2 in word offset 2 "3" - Place word nr.2 in word offset 3 etc... NOTE: in WORD 2 exsits, WORD2_OFFSET > WORD1_OFFSET should be applied.

When timeout mechanism is supported in h/w (currently not), this register contains MEM_PENDING_TIMEOUT_PERIOD[29:0] that specify the time in AOD counter cycles between socket gets pending to socket expiry event (pending timeout duration).
1 - MMU Bypass mode: it is FW responsibility to allocate Pram for incoming TX Packet. 0 - Default mode: it is NAB responsibility to allocate Pram for incoming TX Packet.
A User defined FIFO Group from which NAB obtains a descriptor index when SW_ALLOC_ENABLE=1. Otherwise, Nab obtains desc index from MMU.

A User defined FIFO Index from which NAB obtains a descriptor index when SW_ALLOC_ENABLE=1. Otherwise, Nab obtains desc index from MMU. Elaboration: S/W Allocation is descriptor-index based. Each descriptor is mapped directly to a flat memory which contains a full sized packet (2KiB). This means that every packet consumes the same memory. A pool of free descriptors, and therefore, their associated memory packets are also available, is managed by a specially designated free descriptor index FIFO. Therefore, allocation is made by reading the FIFO and obtaining a real descriptor index (if the FIFO is empty, a null index is returned). Deallocation is done by writing to the FIFO a descriptor index to be freed.

indicated the maximun index of socket ID. implies on number of sockets (Nab POV) in the device. In case host request data comand (send(), recv() etc..) with socket ID bigger than this value, device responses w/ EBADF. Explicitly: 0 - socket 0 is can be issued by host 1 - sockets 0 and 1 can be issued by host 2 - sockets 0,1 and 2 can be issued by host 3 - sockets 0,1,2 and 3 can be issued by host .. .. .. 31 - sockets 0,1,2...,30,31 can be issued by host

A bit per socket indicating this socket has been timeout. Set by H/W upon a PENDING socket reached it's timeout period. Reset by S/W upon data arrives to this socket or when it whishes to flush it. NOTE: when this bit set, H/W will keep socket in PENDING state even if it rx data FIFO is not empty.

This number is the nab to host FIFO threshold. All reads issued to (by host) FIFO are stalled untill FIFO is filled above this threshold. Once the threshold reached FIFO is being read regardless of the threshold. Effective in RCV case only. The motivation is to avoid FIFO underflow. in Osprey (BSD_BYPASS = 1) this threshold is not applicable. The reason for that is that unlike SPI, in SDIO, we have back-pressure in the form of scmdaccept. The SDIO can store SDIO block and can bare the wait-states while waiting till Nab is ready to be read.

cyns response policy for active (cnysable) sockets: 0 - fix priority: selects socket with the lowest index. 1 - round robin priority: lowest index from last selected. Prevents socket starvation. default is fixed priority (0)

The value designates a signed 16 bit value to be added (or decremented if negative) to a given socket's Rx byte count. The NAB would update the relevant Rx byte count safely using MEM_RX_BYTE_COUNTER_SMPHR. Protocol: 1. The S/W determines the size to be added to the Rx byte count, once a new packet arrives to the pipe. 2. The S/W then writes to this register the value comprising both the socket (MEM_RX_BYTE_CNTR_INC_SD) and number to add (MEM_RX_BYTE_CNTR_INC_VAL). 3. NAB H/W safely updates the socket entry.

Socket 0 to 15 state register: bit [2x+1:2x] = "00" - Socket x is IDLE "01" - Socket x is Pending "10" - Socket x is Active "11" - N.A Pending state occurs when blocking socket recives host request and related Rx FIFO is empty. Active state occurs when pending socket recives data or pending-timeout occurs. Active means that the socket is applicable for CNYS. NOTE: 1. Socket that is not pending and not active is considered to be IDLE, i.e. ready to receive host request. 2. S/W can write this reg. This enable restoring socket state after ELP. writing less than a byte is not allowed. 3. If socket is written by S/W as PENDING it will be considered as if no timeout was enabled (we cannot restore a socket to PENDING with timeout period on).

Socket 16 to 31state register: bit [2x+1:2x] = "00" - Socket 16+x is IDLE "01" - Socket 16+x is Pending "10" - Socket 16+x is Active "11" - N.A Pending state occurs when blocking socket recives host request and related Rx FIFO is empty. Active state occurs when pending socket recives data or pending-timeout occurs. Active means that the socket is applicable for CNYS. NOTE: 1. Socket that is not pending and not active is considered to be IDLE, i.e. ready to receive host request. 2. S/W can write this reg. This enable restoring socket state after ELP. writing less than a byte is not allowed. 3. If socket is written by S/W as PENDING it will be considered as if no timeout was enabled (we cannot restore a socket to PENDING with timeout period on).

0 - loopback mode is disabled 1 - loopback mode is enabled In Loopback mode any word written by host to nab via data ocp slave port is returned back to host. Nab pushes the incoming word straight to FIFO toward host.

0 - loopback word swap is disabled 1 - loopback word swap is enabled when loopback mode is enabled, nab examines the host incoming words and search for a pre defined pattern. Once this pattern is detected, it is swapped (16 LSB and 16 MSB are swiched) before pushing it back to host like any other word. The pre define pattern, `LOOPBACK_WORD, can be found in wsoc_nab_defines.v e.g. word pattern: 0x76543210 host stream to nab: ...,0x49a9, 0x5, 0x8675d, 0x7653b, 0x76543210, 0x6745b3c, 0x65d,... nab stream back to host: ...,0x49a9, 0x5, 0x8675d, 0x7653b, 0x32107654, 0x6745b3c, 0x65d,...
1 - FLUSH command 0 - CLOSE command

Bit per socket that supports Both FLUSH and CLOSE commands request (according to MEM_FLUSH_CLOSE_SEL) settings at the time of the request: Set to "1" by SW as request to flush or close request (one at a time), possibly to more than one socket. Set to "0" by H/W once command is completed FLUSH: Once set by S/W Nab looks for the nearest opportunity to clear it, indicating that the socket is flushed. The nearest opportunity is as follow: in case socket is occupied - wait till it clears. In case socket is not occupied and not pending - the socket can be "Flushed" immediately. Nab Clears the semaphore and triggers S/W with flush_close IRQ. In case socket is not occupied but is pending - the socket cannot be "Flushed" immediately. Nab moves the socket to active and waits for host CNYS. Once arrived, answer the CNYS with Disallowed (and not ENODATAC), clears the semaphore and triggers S/W with flush_close IRQ. NOTE: it is NWP S/W responsibility to disallowed the socket before flushing it. CLOSE: Once set by S/W Nab looks for the nearest opportunity to clear it, indicating that the socket is closed. The nearest opportunity is as follow: in case socket is occupied - wait till it clears. In case socket is not occupied - the socket can be "Closed" immediately. Nab Clears the semaphore and triggers S/W with flush_close IRQ. NOTE: it is NWP S/W responsibility to close socket only if it is in IDLE state (and after closing the socket, i.e. setting "111...", in socket jump table).

Interrupt status bits - Masked according to NAB_IRQ_ERR_MASK. ERR Interrupt list: 0 - Tx detect_overflow (snd_abort) ; SEVERE transport error. Overflow at Host Tx bus (host to Device transport). Indication from uper layer outside Nab 1 - Rx detect_underflow ; SEVERE transport error. Underflow at Host Rx bus (Device to host transport). gost FIFO is empty recv transport. 2 - Tx common_err_einval ; SEVERE request failure: Tx Invalid Len, t.len < 4 or t.len < 8 when tcw is present 3 - Tx common_err_ebadlen ; SEVERE request failure: Tx Incompatible Len, desc_len != user payload len (calculated from t.len) or user payload len == 0 4 - Tx common_err_ebaduserlens ; SEVERE request failure: Tx Bad User Len, desc_len >= 32K or equal to 0 5 - Tx sw_alloc_failure ; SEVERE mem resource failure: SW address is not free - semaphore violation 6 - Rx common_err_einval ; SEVERE request failure: Rx Invalid Len, t.len != 4 or t.len != 8 when tcw is present 7 - Rx common_err_ebaduserlenr ; SEVERE request failure: Rx Bad User Len, desc_len >= 32K or equal to 0 8 - Rx detect_cmd_violation ; SEVERE generic CMD failure: commands arrives while mailbox is occupied with previous command and not yet cleared by S/W
Interrupt status clear bits. (clear on WR "1") bit x clears interrupt nr. x. refer to NAB_IRQ_ERR_STATUS_MASKED register for err inrerrupts list

Information saved for the ERR interrupt: 0 - snd_abort ; transfer_op_len 1 - Rx detect_underflow ; {30'b0,recv,recvfrom} (bits 1:0 are used for opcode decode)* 2 - Tx common_err_einval ; tx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 3 - Tx common_err_ebadlen ; tx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 4 - Tx common_err_ebaduserlens ; tx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 5 - Tx sw_alloc_failure ; tx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 6 - Rx common_err_einval ; rx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 7 - Rx common_err_ebaduserlenr ; rx_desc_config (bits 23:22 are taken for opcode decode)* 8 - Rx detect_cmd_violation ; transfer_op_len where, transport_op_len[15:0] - Host opcode transport_op_len[31:16] - Host length desc_config_word[15:0] - User Length desc_config_word[20:16] - Socket ID desc_config_word[31:24] - Flags * rx_desc_config_word[23:22] opcode decode: 0 - cnys, 1 - recvfrom(), 2 - recv() * tx_desc_config_word[23:22] opcode decode: 1 - sendto() , 2 - send() NOTE: snd_abort is relevant only if snd aborts during snd
Indicated Last Unmasked Interrupt index. index x states interrupt nr. x refer to NAB_IRQ_ERR_STATUS_MASKED register for err inrerrupts list

bitfield.description: Bit per socket. Indicates for which sockets, the NAB shall monitor their Rx FIFO, and when they become non-empty, shall trigger the select-response monitor IRQ
Bit per soket. Indicates which sockets shall be denied recv/recvfrom requests with EINEXESELECT error.
Bit per Socket. Indicate which monitored(!) sockets have non-zero Rx FIFO. (note that monitored sockets are configured in MEM_SRP_SKT_MONITORED_VEC)

Reflects the Rx status word current value (dynamic Read). Nothing automatic occurs upon this read. This RX status word is similiar to the one that exist in the Nab response header (that is used in BSD_BYPASS=0 bt the host driver) with the following exceptions: 0to15 - rx byte counter[15:0] - In OSPREY (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 1 by design) - The number of byte counter in socket. Managed by Nab H/W. Not in Osprey (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 0 by design) - Unused. equal to 0. 16to23 - num_of_tx_blk[7:0] - In OSPREY (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 1 by design) - The RX_STATUS_OVERRIDE_ENABLE will be set and S/W will place here the "Tx result Table index". Not in Osprey (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 0 by design) - Remaining Tx Blocks in the Tx chain (in PRAM). Based on MMU H/W indications. 24to28 - num_of_tx_desc[4:0] - In OSPREY (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 1 by design) - The RX_STATUS_OVERRIDE_ENABLE will be set and S/W will place here the "Event size" (payload+ status). Not in Osprey (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 0 by design) - Remaining of Virtual Descriptors in the Tx chain (in PRAM). Based on MMU H/W indications. 29 - ev_rc - In OSPREY (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 1 by design) - Unused. equal to 0. ( No "event receive" indication. The HINT register will be used for signaling to the host). Not in Osprey (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 0 by design) - event receive indication. Signaling the host for pending Event or pending receive socket. 30to31 - event_id[1:0] - In OSPREY (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 1 by design) - The RX_STATUS_OVERRIDE_ENABLE will be set and S/W will place here the "Event ID" (Event Counter modulo 4). Not in Osprey (parameter BSD_BYPASS is equal to 0 by design) - Unused. equal to 0.

Reflects the Rx status word current value (dynamic Read). and automatically latch the value in RX_STATUS_LATCHED. Usage: SDIO Wrapper reads this location and send the read value toward the host. For bit field description refer to RX_STATUS. This register is valid only in BSD_BYPASS=1 (Osprey).

Reflects the Rx status word latched value (static Read). Nothing automatically occurs upon this read. Usage: S/W reads this location in order to know what value has been delivered to Host by SDIO Wrapper. For bit field description refer to RX_STATUS. This register is valid only in BSD_BYPASS=1 (Osprey).

Host interrupt status clear-on-read register Clears all bits of upon read. Usage: host reads the IRQ register which is automatically getting cleared by H/W Osprey Note: The endianness correction and word-size correction are done in SDIO(WSPI) H/W.
